title: AgentSynth: Scalable Task Generation for Generalist Computer-Use Agents
claim: A persona-seeded loop of generate, execute, verify and revise subtasks builds long-horizon tasks whose difficulty is set by how many subtasks are summarized.
layout: Top-down flowchart with side examples, loop arrow, screenshot strip, and fan-out to difficulty levels
description: A vertical flowchart of teal boxes runs down the left: Persona, Initial task, Follow-up subtask, a Yes/No verification branch, Revised subtask description, and Final tasks. Lavender labels name each stage, such as initial task generation, follow-up task generation, verify, summarize, and summarize the sequence. A large light-teal loop arrow returns to follow-up generation, marked ×n. Peach boxes on the right give a concrete example at each step, from a senator persona to a detailed spreadsheet and chart task. Below, a row of four desktop screenshots shows the initial state, initial task, follow-up task 1, and follow-up task n, linked by arrows. At the bottom, arrows fan out from these to task difficulty levels 1 through n+1. The eye starts at the Persona box at the top.
caption: AgentSynth data generation pipeline. Given a persona, the task proposer generates an initial task, which is followed by a sequence of subtasks executed by the agent. Each step is verified; if execution fails, a revised subtask description is generated. After n successful steps, a summarization agent composes final high-level tasks. Tasks at different difficulty levels are formed by summarizing the first 1 to n subtasks, enabling controllable task complexity.
abstract: We introduce AgentSynth, a scalable and cost-efficient pipeline for automatically synthesizing high-quality tasks and trajectory datasets for generalist computer-use agents. Leveraging information asymmetry, AgentSynth constructs subtasks that are simple during generation but significantly more challenging when composed into long-horizon tasks, enabling the creation of over 6,000 diverse and realistic tasks. A key strength of AgentSynth is its ability to precisely modulate task complexity by varying the number of subtasks. Empirical evaluations show that state-of-the-art LLM agents suffer a steep performance drop, from 18% success at difficulty level 1 to just 4% at level 6, highlighting the benchmark's difficulty and discriminative power. Moreover, our pipeline achieves a low average cost of $0.60 per trajectory, orders of magnitude cheaper than human annotations. Our code and data are available at https://github.com/sunblaze-ucb/AgentSynth
